skill.name: baoyu-compress-image
skill.description: Local image compression for single files or directories. Converts to WebP by default, supports PNG and JPEG outputs, and selects available image tools.
skill.summary: Compress local images to WebP, PNG, or JPEG with quality controls and batch processing.
skill.author: jimliu

security_audit.summary: The executable script has legitimate image-compression behavior, but it performs native command execution through child_process and PATH-resolved tools. Most template-literal and Markdown backtick detections are false positives, while hidden EXTEND.md loading and destructive default replacement create real workflow risks.

remediation.issue: External image tools are executed through PATH-resolved command names.
remediation.suggestion: Use a fixed allowlist, resolve trusted absolute paths, document required binaries, and avoid executing unexpected tools from PATH.

remediation.issue: Hidden EXTEND.md files can override skill behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic hidden-file loading or require explicit user opt-in. Never allow extension content to override safety instructions.

remediation.issue: Original images can be replaced by default.
remediation.suggestion: Default to preserving source files and require an explicit replace flag for destructive writes, especially during recursive processing.

remediation.issue: Usage examples rely on automatic package execution with npx -y.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned local dependency or require users to install Bun explicitly before running the skill.

finding_verdicts.reason: The dynamic import target is the literal package name "sharp", not user-controlled input. It is used as an image compression fallback, not arbitrary code loading.

The code spawns the system which command to detect compressors. The command names are controlled by the script, but this still depends on PATH lookup and external process execution.
runCmd spawns sips, cwebp, or convert with file paths supplied through CLI options. Arguments are not passed through a shell, but external native tools are executed on user-selected files.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Vector Through EXTEND.md
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells agents to load project and home EXTEND.md files before the workflow, then says extension content overrides defaults. A hidden or project-local Markdown file could inject unsafe workflow instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The extension behavior is explicitly documented, including hidden paths and override semantics. The risk is contextual because the script itself does not implement the loader.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Image Replacement by Default
semantic_findings.description: The script defaults keep to false and processFile can delete or overwrite the source image when writing output. Recursive use can therefore cause unintended data loss.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default option sets keep to false, and the file processing path deletes or renames over outputs. The behavior is also described in the user-facing command examples.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Runtime Installation in Usage Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The command examples use npx with automatic confirmation to run Bun. Agents following these instructions may download and execute package-managed tooling without an explicit user review step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples clearly use npx -y bun in multiple workflow commands. The security impact depends on the user environment and package manager configuration.

content.value_statement: Large image files slow handoffs and make repositories harder to share. This skill compresses local images to WebP, PNG, or JPEG using available command-line tools.
actual_capabilities: Compresses single image files to WebP by default.
Creates WebP, PNG, or JPEG output with configurable quality.
Processes image directories recursively when requested.
Can keep originals or replace them based on the keep option.
Reports size reduction in plain text or machine-readable output.
Selects available compressors from cwebp, ImageMagick, sips, or Sharp.
limitations: Requires Bun and may rely on external image tools installed on the host.
Default behavior can replace source files unless the keep option is used.
WebP support depends on available compressors and platform capabilities.
It does not sandbox native image parsers for untrusted image files.

use_cases.title: Optimize Web Assets
use_cases.description: Reduce product image and screenshot sizes before committing them to a web project.

use_cases.title: Prepare Documentation Images
use_cases.description: Compress tutorial screenshots while preserving readable visual detail for documentation.

use_cases.title: Batch-Compress Design Exports
use_cases.description: Process a folder of exported mockups with consistent quality and format settings.

prompt_templates.title: Compress One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use baoyu-compress-image to compress ./assets/photo.png to WebP with default quality. Keep the original file.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Format and Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress ./screenshots/homepage.png as PNG at quality 75. Save a separate compressed copy.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress every supported image in ./docs/images recursively. Use WebP output and summarize total size reduction.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Automation Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress ./release-assets recursively at quality 70 and return machine-readable output for a build report.

output_examples.input: Compress photo.png at the default quality.
output_examples.output: Reports that photo.png was converted to photo.webp with original size, output size, reduction percentage, and compressor name.

output_examples.input: Compress screenshots recursively with automation output.
output_examples.output: Returns a structured summary of processed files, total input size, total output size, reduction ratio, and selected compressor.

output_examples.input: Compress screenshot.png as PNG while keeping the original.
output_examples.output: Creates a separate compressed PNG file with a compressed suffix and reports the size reduction.

best_practices: Use the keep option when source images are irreplaceable.
Review visual quality after changing the quality value.
Run recursive compression on a copied folder before processing originals.
anti_patterns: Running recursive compression on original assets without a backup.
Processing untrusted images with native tools outside a sandbox.
Assuming every host has the same compressor installed.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports WebP, PNG, and JPEG output. WebP is the default output format.

faq.question: Does it keep the original image?
faq.answer: The default workflow can replace source files. Use the keep option when you need to preserve originals.

faq.question: Which tools does it use?
faq.answer: It tries cwebp, ImageMagick, macOS sips, or Sharp based on platform and requested format.

faq.question: Can it process folders?
faq.answer: Yes. It can process a directory and can scan nested directories when recursive mode is enabled.

faq.question: Can I use it in automation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can emit machine-readable output that includes per-file results and aggregate size savings.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive images?
faq.answer: Processing is local, but it executes local image tools. Use trusted files and a controlled environment.
